original_question: Based on the development of E. S. Golod’s construction(see, for example, Discrete Math. Appl., 23, no. 5–6(2013), 491–501), for each prime number p, construct a finitely generated residually finite p-group with a non-trivial finite centre. Such groups with infinite and trivial centres are known(see 9.76 and Archive 11.101).
target_in_paper: Problem 21.132 in New Problems (21th issue, 2026): construct, for each prime number p, a finitely generated residually finite p-group with a non-trivial finite centre.
correct_elements: The draft already matches Problem 21.132 almost verbatim: it has the correct quantifier (for each prime p), the correct task (construct), the correct class of groups (finitely generated residually finite p-groups), and the correct unresolved centre condition (finite and non-trivial). It also preserves the paper’s motivating comparison with the known infinite-centre and trivial-centre cases. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the question should define a residually finite p-group as a group G such that for every 1 ≠ g ∈ G there exists a homomorphism from G onto a finite p-group in which the image of g is nontrivial.
It should spell out “non-trivial finite centre” as 1 < |Z(G)| < ∞.
It should make explicit that the construction is required separately for every prime p.
The phrase “Based on the development of E. S. Golod’s construction” is methodological background from Problem 21.132, not an additional structural hypothesis on the output group.

If one imports nearby context, Problem 9.76 defines a Golod group via the adjoint group 1 + F/I, where F is the free algebra without constant term in non-commuting variables over a field of characteristic p > 0 and F/I is a non-nilpotent nil-algebra; however, Problem 21.132 itself does not require the target group to be formally stated in that language. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
refined_question: Using a Golod-type construction in the sense intended by the paper, for each prime number p construct a finitely generated group G such that every element of G has p-power order, for every nonidentity element g ∈ G there exists a homomorphism from G onto a finite p-group whose image of g is nontrivial, and the centre Z(G) is finite and nontrivial; equivalently, 1 < |Z(G)| < ∞.
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Problem 21.132. The surrounding context confirms that this is the precise intended target: Problem 9.76 defines Golod groups and notes that examples with infinite centre are known, while Archive 11.101 records the existence of a Golod group with trivial centre. Therefore the refined question should isolate only the remaining case of a finite nontrivial centre, without broadening the problem beyond the notebook’s formulation. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
